svg.title: Where one crash loop shows up in three different parts of the Kubernetes API
svg.desc: Three stacked panels describe the same failing pod, checkout-3c-aaa, from three separate parts of the Kubernetes API. Each panel puts what the API says on the left of a dashed split and what that source alone would let you conclude on the right. The first panel is the pod status, whose phase is Running; a cross marks the conclusion as true and useless, because a pod in a crash loop is in phase Running. The second panel is the container statuses, and it is the tall one because it carries two rows: the current waiting state, reason CrashLoopBackOff with a restart count of seven, crossed out as the symptom rather than the cause since it only means the kubelet is waiting before trying again; and the previous terminated state with exit code one, the single row in the figure marked with a tick, because that is where the cause lives, describing an instance of the container that is already gone. The third panel is the events, a BackOff seen forty-two times, crossed out as the sequence rather than the cause, with a note that events expire after an hour so an empty list means recently rather than ever. An arrow joins all three into a verdict box at the bottom: a crash loop at high confidence with a restart count of seven, and the next call to make, reading the previous instance's log rather than the current one, because the current instance has logged nothing yet.
svg.text: One crash loop, three places to look
Pod checkout-3c-aaa. Left: what the API says. Right: what that source alone lets you conclude.
A pod in a crash loop is in phase Running.
The waiting reason is the symptom.
It means the kubelet is waiting before trying again.
lastState is where the cause lives.
It describes an instance of the container that is gone.
Alone: the sequence, not the cause.
Events expire after an hour: empty means recently, not ever.
Next call: get_logs(pod_name="checkout-3c-aaa", container="app", previous=True). The current instance has logged nothing yet.
